discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional van der Waals materials and moire quantum matter
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees collapses the electronic bandwidth into nearly flat bands, where interactions dominate. Jarillo-Herrero's group (Nature 2018) realised this by tear-and-stack fabrication with hBN encapsulation, discovering gate-tunable correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity in pure carbon. This established the twist angle as a new, purely geometric control parameter for quantum phases, launching moire quantum matter: correlated and Chern insulators, orbital magnetism, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states, sliding ferroelectricity and moire excitons in graphene and TMD heterostructures. For those of us who treat crystal structure and stacking as design variables, it showed that a single electrostatic gate can switch one device between metal, insulator, magnet and superconductor. It is a clean, controllable mechanism that has transformed condensed-matter physics and opened new device concepts.
